subject: MedCore POC: security follow-up + pen report & vulnerability cadence
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medicore.com>, security@medicore.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: MedCore POC: security follow-up + pen report & vulnerability cadence

Alex / MedCore security team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep the POC timeline moving: 

Recap (from today's discovery):
- Scope: short pilot with model inference of de-identified clinical notes; no PHI storage planned in the initial POC, but some tokenized identifiers may be present in transit.
- Compliance asked: SOC 2 status, GDPR data flows, and HIPAA readiness for future production use.
- Existing security assets mentioned: external vuln scans (monthly?), a red-team/pen test done in 2027-03 (you mentioned a report), and an internal risk matrix (you referenced a spreadsheet).

Redwood asks / next steps: 
1) Can you share the latest pen test report (redacted as needed)? we will need it for our security review and to map CVEs to our runtime mitigations. Please attach a redacted PDF or point to a secure share.
2) SOC 2 status: is there an expected Type II completion date? if not Type II, can you share scope and compensating controls?
3) HIPAA/GDPR: any specific data processing agreements or DPO contact we should work with?
4) Vulnerability management SLA & cadence proposal (we suggest this as a starting point):
   - Critical: acknowledgement within 24 hours, mitigation/patch ETA within 72 hours (or temporary mitigation), full remediation or documented workaround within 14 days.
   - High: acknowledgement 48 hours, remediation plan within 7 days.
   - Medium: acknowledgement 7 days, remediation in 30 days.
   - Low: tracked for next release.
   - Scans: weekly external unauthenticated scan, monthly authenticated scans against staging, quarterly full pen test (or after major changes).

5) Vendor security questionnaire: attached is our lightweight intake form to kick off the questionnaire and access request (redwood-security-intake-form.pdf). Please complete or let us know if you prefer to push your own questionnaire.

6) Permission to share the pen-test redaction with Redwood Security (Neha + Rishi) for a triage read — if an NDA is needed, we can sign one quickly.

Proposed calendar: 30-min technical sync on Tuesday 2027-04-27 10:00 PDT to go through the pen report highlights and remediation owners. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Appended: please also attach the MediCore risk matrix you referenced so we can align severity definitions (MediCore-RiskMatrix-v1.xlsx).

Thanks — David

--
David Kim
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
https://www.redwood.inference
(415) 555-0198
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medicore.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@medicore.com, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedCore POC: security follow-up + pen report & vulnerability cadence

David — thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the concrete SLAs and proposed cadence. Quick responses inline: 

1) Pen test: attaching a redacted copy of the March 2027 assessment (MedCore-pen-test-redacted-2027-03.pdf). We removed PII and exploit code; we can provide more detail under NDA.
2) SOC 2: we completed Type I earlier this year; Type II is expected by end of Q3 2027 (we'll share the timeline and scope once our compliance lead signs off).
3) HIPAA/GDPR: we already have a BAA template and a GDPR DPA; DPO is Priya Singh (priya.singh@medicore.com). For the POC, we consider compensating controls acceptable but will document them.
4) Vulnerability SLAs: we can commit to acknowledgement within 48 hours and a remediation ETA for Critical issues within 72 hours for P0/P1 items. For POC scope we typically target monthly authenticated scans; quarterly full-scope pen-tests are on our roadmap but may be annual depending on budget.

We'll review Redwood's intake form and get it back to you by EOD tomorrow. Happy to meet 2027-04-27 10:00 PDT — works for our engineering lead (cc'd: security@medicore.com).

Attachments: MedCore-pen-test-redacted-2027-03.pdf

Cheers,
Alex Morgan
Head of Product Operations
MediCore Health
alex.morgan@medicore.com
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MedCore POC: security follow-up + pen report & vulnerability cadence

Team — forwarding Alex's response and the redacted pen-test. Please treat the attachment as TLP:AMBER for now. A few asks before the sync: 

- Quick triage requested: scan the attached PDF for any references to high/critical CVEs we should call out in the meeting. Flag anything we consider a blocker for hosted inference (admin auth, token handling, KV cache exposure, etc.).
- Confirm whether the proposed SLAs are acceptable from our side for a POC. We should aim to avoid taking on more than an acknowledgement + escalation window for Critical items in the contract.
- If you need an NDA for fuller report access, tell me the minimum template language and I'll request it from MedCore.

Proposed internal prep: compile 1 page of top 5 technical questions and suggested mitigations for the sync. I'll add those to the invite.

Thanks — David

Date: 2027-04-27T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MedCore POC: security follow-up + pen report & vulnerability cadence

David / Rishi — I pulled the redacted report and skimmed for high-level items. Top-of-mind notes before the sync: 

1) CVE mapping: the report references three CVEs in the web app stack — two are marked high and look exploitable without MFA on admin paths. Please confirm whether the admin portal is in scope for the POC. If so, we'll require an interim mitigation (IP allowlist or MFA) prior to enabling production traffic.
2) Scanning cadence: monthly authenticated + weekly external unauthenticated is reasonable for a POC; ask MedCore to provide proofs of remediation (ticket links or PRs) for any high/critical items they claim to have fixed.
3) SOC 2: Type II by end Q3 is acceptable, but we should capture compensating controls in the contract for the pilot (encryption-at-rest, logging retention, incident response contact).
4) NDA: we can sign a mutual NDA; I'll draft a short addendum that limits sharing of full report to named reviewers (Neha, Rishi, and Redwood infra eng lead).

Prep items I can take: list of CVEs with recommended mitigations and suggested contract language around remediation SLAs + evidence requirements. Rishi — can you pull our standard POC security checklist and any minimal contract redlines?

Neha
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
